011. Skew estimation

Length-weighted median of Hough segments folded mod 90 gives +0.000°. Rejected outright if |angle| exceeds max_skew_deg.

Implemented in

src/schematic2netlist/preprocess.py:121 _estimate_skew()

Config

Output

ink_px25220
A wrong angle here rotates every downstream coordinate. If the estimate is 0.000 on a visibly skewed page, Hough found too few long segments -- lower hough_min_line_frac.

099. Gap bridging

Line-kernel closings join stroke fragments across pen lifts. Components 24 → 12. Magenta = pixels this stage invented.

Output

THE STAGE TO SUSPECT FIRST FOR WELDED NETS. A horizontal closing bridges horizontal gaps between ANY ink, so two side-by-side VERTICAL rails closer than bridge_span fuse into one conductor. That is why the span is 7 and not the 18 it shipped with. If deleted_px is non-zero the kernel is even-length and the closing is destroying ink (bridge_odd_kernel).

1010. Noise-blob filter

A blob survives on area OR extent — a hairline wire has small area but large extent, and an area-only rule shatters nets. Red = dropped.

1414. Net assembly (crossover)

13 electrical nets, one colour each. At each detected Wire Crossover box (magenta, 2 here) the wires are notched apart and opposite arms reconnected, so a crossing does not weld two nets.

relink='angle' samples a ring and pairs the most-opposite arms by measured direction; 'band' votes in four fixed strips at the box edges and is placement-dependent -- a 2 px box shift once took terminal-pair F1 from 1.000 to 0.523.

2122. WHERE the topology is wrong

Red = terminal on a node that carries two or more DIFFERENT ground-truth nets (welded, and the offending conductor is painted red too). Blue = its net is split across several nodes. Green = correct. 13 welded, 2 split, 15 correct.

Implemented in

Output

terminals_split2
terminals_correct15
welded_nodes5
split_gt_nets3
Red conductors are where to look. Trace one back through stage 9 (bridging) and stage 14 (net assembly): if the red region is a long rail touching several components, the weld is upstream in the ink; if it is a compact blob at a crossing, the notch/relink decision is at fault.
